why: I20's contract (tests_m2/test_extracted_refinement.py clause 3, preregistered at 8839b7d, an ancestor of this prereg 0672e65; its outputs merged at 04e2293, after this prereg's base f8fa447) adds two SORT-width laws to M2 (L_sort_width_batchheadercodecv0_144_1abeb29c, _166_8ad80b42), decided by holon.sorts.width over the extracted model and UNKNOWN. Their records name no model (artifacts has no 'model' key: holon run builds no Bend model of their document under gen/M2/model). The contract makes every UNKNOWN record eligible and TestRealM2 picks every UNKNOWN M2 record at run time (so that a later re-derivation breaks nothing), so real_wrong_proof raised KeyError 'model' on them before any intake ran, for every implementation (evidence: test_a_stale_statement_hash_is_refused at 8d9f02d). For a record without artifacts.model the proof now imports the model holon would name after the law's facts document (holon.mpipeline.model_name: the document's stem, non-word characters as _, plus .bend); the regenerated tree holds neither that model nor a law file for such a law, so the kernel refuses it. Every record with a model is handled as before, and no assertion changes.

The rename map sent Root to ZqOld and RootNew to ZqNew, which reverses the order of the two getters (Root < RootNew, ZqNew < ZqOld). Rule P4 names a PAR-weak law and orders its claim's two sides by the getters' names, so no derivation can satisfy the test under that map: the prereg instrument itself (tests_m3/_i24x.py::expected, run on the renamed copy exactly as the test builds it) derives L_par_weak_HdrBytes_ZqNew_HdrBytes_ZqOld_v2 where the renamed original law id is L_par_weak_HdrBytes_ZqOld_HdrBytes_ZqNew_v2, and every other law agrees. The one change: RootNew now maps to ZqOldNew, an order-preserving renaming (Root < RootNew and ZqOld < ZqOldNew); under it the instrument's two derivations agree law for law and statement for statement. The other renamings, the fixture, the derivation and every assertion are unchanged; the test still renames the Solidity functions (enc_x, load_x), the record fields and the Go methods (Root, RootNew, makeV2).

F30: the I30 merge (4085005) moved M3 from holon-rules/1.1 (I24: PAR only) to holon-rules/1.2 (the same PAR producer objects plus I30's typed SORT), as both preregistered contracts require (tests_m3/test_derive_par.py::TestRegistry::test_catalogs, tests_m3/test_sort_types.py). A holon-ir/0.3 statement hash covers rule_catalog_version, so all 80 PAR statement hashes changed although no claim did, and G2's statement-change tie (I10, audit F-M2-08) needs one accepted laws/STATEMENT_DIFF.jsonl entry per changed law: F30 appends 80 catalog_rederivation lines, each new statement an M3 law under holon-rules/1.2. The preregistered assertion forbade every line with new.milestone == 'M3', at HEAD and forever, so once M3's catalog moved no tree could satisfy both it and the tie. Its docstring states its purpose (P11): no earlier law is about the linked codec document, so DERIVATION links is [] and I24 appends no line. The amended test keeps links == [] unchanged and forbids (1) every link line naming an M3 law: a cross_milestone entry, or any entry pairing an M3 law with another law (another id or another milestone), since pairs come only from links, which are []; and (2) every line whose new statement is an M3 law under I24's catalog (tests_m3/_i24.py CATALOG_VERSION, holon-rules/1.1), which every line I24 could append is: on I24's tree, where catalog_version('M3') was holon-rules/1.1 and every M3 law carried it, a line about an M3 law is forbidden exactly as before. It stops forbidding only lines whose new statement is an M3 law under a later catalog (later keys' statement changes, such as these catalog re-derivations), which G2 checks. No other assertion, fixture or instrument changes.

Build review M1: rule T2's text checks could be bypassed in Lean. A def named with an escaped identifier containing a block-comment opener (def «/-» ... def «-/») hides the code between from tests_m3/_i42.py::lean_code and from holon.lean.strip_comments (so from check_text's forbidden scan too), e.g. a macro_rules that rewrites `=`; Lean then accepts weakened theorems whose text still equals the frozen statements (the reviewer's demo checked, with cor_6_5_potentials elaborated to True). The check now also refuses any escaped identifier after the marker and applies holon.lean.FORBIDDEN to this contract's own comment-free reading. Stricter only: the committed Theory.lean has no escaped identifier and passes; a new test (test_lean_elaborated_types_are_the_frozen_ones, not preregistered) compares each frozen theorem's elaborated type under pp.all. holon.lean.strip_comments itself is in the holon-ir/0.2 and 0.3 generator closures, so it is reported for the lead, not changed here.

Build review M2: rule T7's text checks could be bypassed in Bend. They strip `#...` comments line by line without regard to string literals, so a record pattern after a "#" string in a one-line match was invisible, and a helper opening the record proved per-edge facts by computation while dead `_a = avail_0(h)` lines satisfied the naming check (the reviewer's demo passed bend, --verdict and this test). The check now refuses string and char literals in an instance PROOF.bend (so `#` always starts a comment) and requires each bridge_* body to be exactly `match h:`, one record case, `{==}`. Stricter only: the committed proofs have no literal and their bridges have that form.

Build review M2 (the same hole as rule T7's): the canary PROOF.bend's record checks read lines with `#...` removed regardless of strings; the check now refuses string and char literals there too, so `#` always starts a comment. Stricter only: the committed canary proofs have none.

I43's contract (tests_m3/test_lean_promoted.py rule L8, preregistered at the I43 prereg; human answer Q8: every PROVED law is promoted to Lean; BUILD_PLAN I43: 'Records gain I2') adds one lean4 kernel entry to every attempted record of results/M1, results/M2 and results/M2/extracted_m1 (their PROVED laws and the REFUTED counter-laws over the machine kinds) and sets independence_class to I2 exactly when that entry is checked. The preregistered assertion let only filter_bin, concretization and generator_sha256 (and keys named seconds) differ from the I40 prereg in the M0-M2 records, so no tree could satisfy both it and I43-R5 and I43-P1 to P3. The amended test keeps everything else: every other field still equals the I40 prereg's; kernels may only gain exactly one lean4 entry, the earlier entries unchanged and in order (no record had a lean4 entry there but M0's, which I43 does not regenerate); independence_class may only change from I1-shared to I2, and only when that entry's result is checked, else it is unchanged; at least one record still carries a recomputed bin. It is amended in the I43 prereg commit itself (the first review of the I43 prereg, minor m4), so the I43 build edits no test.

The comparison of an UNKNOWN record with its prereg version (62fb13d) failed only because other keys' statement-lifecycle changes moved the three PAR-weak records after the prereg: I27's holon-rules/1.3 and I31's holon-rules/1.4 re-derivations changed statement_hash (and non_vacuity.parent_statement_hash, its copy), each logged as a catalog_rederivation line of laws/STATEMENT_DIFF.jsonl. The amended check accepts a moved statement_hash only when a chain of logged entries for that law leads from the prereg's hash to HEAD's, and non_vacuity only when it differs in that copy alone; every other field must still be the prereg's, so a change I40 made still fails.
